feed.title: Quantitative Markets & Institutions Lab — Research
feed.subtitle: Independent, evidence-led research on financial models, market regimes, institutions, and investor decisions.

entry.title: Why do the same assets behave differently when the environment changes?
entry.summary: A historical scenario framework connecting activity, inflation, liquidity, institutional response, and fragile model assumptions without classifying the present.

entry.title: Why can stocks and bonds fall together?
entry.summary: A long-form synthesis examining a stock–bond correlation shift alongside diversification, portfolio construction, and historical risk-model monitoring.

entry.title: Can an “optimal” portfolio stay optimal?
entry.summary: Why a maximum-Sharpe portfolio’s estimated advantage degraded—and what risk-based methods did and did not fix.

entry.title: Does a 95% risk estimate fail only 5% of the time?
entry.summary: A rolling historical VaR forecast produced too many breaches, and the exceptions clustered.

entry.title: Will bonds diversify stocks in the next stress?
entry.summary: Stock–bond correlation changed sign in the studied sample, exposing the regime assumption inside diversification.

entry.title: Does a factor fund deliver the exposure on its label?
entry.summary: The advertised exposures appeared, but no alpha survived the multiple-testing threshold.

entry.title: Can one volatility number describe every option?
entry.summary: Observed volatility, fat tails, and an implied-volatility skew reject the constant-volatility Gaussian fingerprints.

entry.title: How many simulations are enough?
entry.summary: Monte Carlo accuracy depends on a declared tolerance, sampling variance, and the numerical bias the path count cannot cure.
